title: Decimals on the Number Line: Comparing, Ordering and Rounding
seo_title: Grade 4 Comparing and Rounding Decimals Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Plot decimal numbers with tenth decimal part on the number line; compare and order decimal numbers with decimal parts to hundredths; round decimal numbers to the nearest whole number and to the nearest tenth.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets on comparing, ordering and rounding decimals for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: number lines, comparing, ordering, rounding and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the decimal points, then compare place by place.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • On a number line from 0 to 1 split into 10 equal parts, each part is 0.1.
  • To compare decimals, line up the decimal points. Compare the ones, then the tenths, then the hundredths. Write 0.8 as 0.80 to compare with 0.75.
  • A decimal with more digits is not always bigger: 0.8 > 0.75.
  • To round to the nearest whole number, look at the tenths digit. To round to the nearest tenth, look at the hundredths digit. 5 or more: round up. Less than 5: round down.

Examples

Example

Compare 0.8 and 0.75

0.80 and 0.75

8 tenths > 7 tenths

Answer: 0.8 > 0.75

Example

Round 4.65 to the nearest tenth

hundredths digit 5

Answer: 4.7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
More digits means bigger0.75 < 0.8.
Comparing 8 and 75Write 0.8 as 0.80 first.
Rounding 5 down5 or more rounds up.

faq.q: How do I round 3.96 to the nearest tenth?
faq.a: The hundredths digit is 6, so round up: 3.96 ≈ 4.0.
